question: What is the drainage pattern of the rivers originating from the Northern Plains?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dendritic**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The drainage pattern of rivers originating from the Northern Plains is **Dendritic.**
 
• **Dendritic drainage** resembles the branches of a tree, where tributaries join the main river at acute angles.
 
• This pattern develops in regions with a homogeneous substratum where the river flows over flat terrain, such as the Northern Plains of India.
 
• Rivers like the Ganga, Yamuna, and Brahmaputra exhibit dendritic drainage systems due to the plain topography and uniform rock structure.
 
• The dendritic pattern is one of the most common drainage systems globally and is indicative of stable geological conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Drainage Patterns:**

 
 
• **Trellis:** Forms when tributaries join the main river at right angles, often in regions with alternating hard and soft rock layers.
 
• **Radial:** Develops when rivers flow outward from a central elevated point, such as a volcanic cone or dome.
 
• **Centripetal:** Occurs when rivers converge towards a central depression or basin.
 
 
 
• **Northern Plains Rivers:**
 
 
• Fed by Himalayan snowmelt, rainfall, and underground aquifers, ensuring perennial flow.
 
• Examples include major rivers like Ganga, Yamuna, Brahmaputra, and their tributaries.
 
 
 
• **Geological Features:**
 
 
• The Northern Plains are formed by the alluvial deposits of the Indo-Gangetic Basin.
 
• Flat terrain and fertile soil make this region suitable for dendritic drainage.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Drainage Patterns:**
 
 
• Drainage patterns provide insights into the topography, geological structure, and hydrological processes of a region.
 
• They influence agriculture, water resource management, and ecosystem stability.
